item.title: Resto van harte 20 jarig jubileum Goede doelen 10 september 2026 Anderhalf jaar geleden ging Marcel met pensioen. Hij zocht een leuke activiteit en wilde graag nieuwe mensen uit zijn buurt leren kennen. Lees meer
item.description:
Anderhalf jaar geleden ging Marcel met pensioen. Hij zocht een leuke activiteit en wilde graag nieuwe mensen uit zijn buurt leren kennen. Tijdens het uitlaten van zijn hond raakte hij aan de praat met een paar buurtgenoten. Zij vertelden enthousiast over Resto VanHarte. Marcel besloot een keer mee te gaan. Inmiddels schuift hij iedere dinsdagavond aan bij Resto VanHarte in Amsterdam Zuidoost Holendrecht. “Ik wil geen avond missen, want het is echt een feestje.” 

donderdag 10 september 2026 - Goede doelen

Meteen onderdeel van de familie 

Vanaf zijn eerste bezoek voelt Marcel zich welkom. “De koks, vrijwilligers en gasten zijn allemaal even persoonlijk en warm. Ik was gelijk onderdeel van de familie.” 

Die gezelligheid blijft niet aan tafel. Marcel komt regelmatig andere gasten tegen in de buurt. “Dan hebben we elkaar meteen wat te vertellen. Zo voel ik me nog meer verbonden met de buurt.” 

Dat is precies wat samen eten kan doen. Je deelt niet alleen een maaltijd, maar ook verhalen en mooie momenten. Zo ontstaan nieuwe contacten. En soms zelfs vriendschappen. 

Een avond vol aandacht 

Bij Resto VanHarte draait het daarom om meer dan lekker eten. Vrijwilligers zorgen voor een warm welkom en een fijne sfeer. 

Dat merkt Marcel iedere week. “Een van de vrijwilligers heet ons altijd welkom met een praatje en neemt het menu door. Zijn vrouw speelt vaak een stuk piano voor ons. En laatst had een vrijwilliger van het buurthuis heerlijke Surinaamse bara’s meegenomen. Het is echt genieten.” 

Resto VanHarte organiseert dit soort diners op veel plekken in Nederland. Iedereen is welkom. Zo brengt de organisatie buurtbewoners bij elkaar en helpt ze eenzaamheid te verminderen. Mede dankzij de deelnemers van de Postcode Loterij kan Resto VanHarte in steeds meer buurten mensen samenbrengen.

item.title: NewsStudy reveals only 30% of South African Publishers Block AI Crawlers despite widespread fair use concerns A new study, Protocol Gap: South Africa, reveals that only a third of publishers in South Africa are actively aiming to limit AI crawler access to their content using robots.txt; these are files that allow a site owner to tell search engine crawlers which URLs they can access on the site, and which ones they should avoid. The new data from South Africa reveals that these AI-blocking measures are concentrated among larger and better-resourced publishers while smaller outlets remain widely exposed to scraping – the same outlets whose sustainability is most at risk due to declining traffic and referrals.
item.description:
Press Releases

A new study, Protocol Gap: South Africa, reveals that only a third of publishers in South Africa are actively aiming to limit AI crawler access to their content using robots.txt; these are files that allow a site owner to tell search engine crawlers which URLs they can access on the site, and which ones they should avoid. The new data from South Africa reveals that these AI-blocking measures are concentrated among larger and better-resourced publishers while smaller outlets remain widely exposed to scraping – the same outlets whose sustainability is most at risk due to declining traffic and referrals.

Over the last year, South Africa’s leading news sites have lost an average of 20% of their daily page views, mirroring international dynamics. As extraction and use of publisher content by AI companies increases, often without compensation or attribution, it accelerates visibility issues that threaten the survival of newsrooms – in South Africa and beyond.

In late 2025, the South African Competition Commission concluded a landmark Media and Digital Platforms Market Inquiry (MDPMI), which found that publishers are increasingly being forced to make trade-offs between maintaining visibility and protecting their content.  In this context, use of robots.txt is one indicator of how publishers are responding to growing pressure to decide whether and how their content can be accessed by automated crawlers. The Protocol Gap report’s findings contribute to ongoing debates in South Africa’s media sector on application of competition law, copyright reform, and the development of a national AI policy framework.

Robots.txt is a text file that can be added to the root domain of a website that contains instructions to search engines and web crawlers about what content they can access. This includes directives to AI bots that systematically browse and collect data to train LLMs and power AI assistants and search engines. Robots.txt is one of the few free tools available to content creators to signal how they want their data to be used by AI companies. While not legally binding, robots.txt has been used in legal complaints against unauthorised crawling and scraping in Canada, US, and UK. The file can serve as leverage in licensing negotiations, especially where AI models rely heavily on large volumes of unconsented, uncompensated data. However, effectiveness depends on voluntary compliance by AI developers, and its role within broader governance frameworks remains contested.

Based on analysis of 263 news websites, Protocol Gap: South Africa finds that while 74.1% of publishers have a robots.txt file in place, only 30.4% block at least one AI crawler as of April 2026. Although the percentage of publishers that use robots.txt to block AI crawlers rose modestly from 29.7% in December 2025 to 30.4%, the findings suggest that most publishers remain open to AI data collection.

Below these broad findings, the study identified a gap in adoption of AI-scraping policies between large and small publishers that reflects disparities in resources, technical capacity, referral traffic dependency, and strategic positioning. This raises important questions about bargaining power, content ownership and sustainability, as AI systems become increasingly reliant on news content. In the absence of clear legal and regulatory frameworks, the decisions publishers make now about how AI crawlers access their content could have long-lasting consequences.

The report, released by the Media Leadership Think Tank (MLTT) at the GIBS Business School (Gordon Institute of Business Science), the Journalism Relay Project, and the International Fund for Public Interest Media (IFPIM) is part of a broader research collaboration focused on Brazil, Indonesia, and South Africa. Through technical and qualitative research, it aims to increase awareness among media organizations on how AI systems access their content and help to inform strategies and policies to manage AI crawlers in ways that best serve newsroom interests. The report includes a detailed methodology for all those who may want to replicate this research on robots.txt in other countries and regions.

The study also provides a replicable methodology for researchers and publisher associations interested in conducting similar audits and concludes with next steps for research and engagement with ongoing efforts to strengthen publisher agency, bargaining power, and transparency in emerging AI licensing ecosystems.

‍

Full suite of Protocol Gap reports: ctrl-j.info/publications

‍

item.title: StoryIn a country under fire, a radio station refuses to let the signal go darkHromadske Radio, one of Ukraine's few independent, non-commercial and non-governmental news and talk radio stations, is among the outlets that have come under attack by Russian forces. Since 2022, nine of its transmitters have been destroyed or seized. It has continued to broadcast anyway, 24/7 across seven FM transmitters, five of them in frontline regions.
item.description:
Press Releases

Paris, 20 August: In Ukraine, reliable information can be a matter of survival, especially for those living on the frontlines. Yet since Russia's full-scale invasion, journalists and the infrastructure they depend on have been deliberately targeted, making the reporting of attacks, troop movements, aid deliveries and reconstruction an immensely dangerous job.

Hromadske Radio, one of Ukraine's few independent, non-commercial and non-governmental news and talk radio stations, is among the outlets that have come under attack. Since 2022, nine of its transmitters have been destroyed or seized by Russian troops.  It has continued to broadcast anyway, 24/7 across seven FM transmitters, five of them in frontline regions.  Their radio broadcasts are particularly meaningful for those on the contact line: when drone strikes take out the power grid, hand-held, battery-powered radios are one of the only channels for audiences in occupied and combat zones to get factual, up-to-date information, much of it essential to their safety and support needs.

Hromadske Radio relayed to IFPIM staff that when Russian shelling has disrupted their ability to broadcast on the frontlines, they have received constant messages from residents hoping for news to be restored.

“Two women from the "red zone" of Kherson called. I spoke with them and you could hear the shelling even over the phone. They complained that they can't hear Hromadske Radio, because they used to wake up and fall asleep with us,” said Ruslana Brianska, Executive Director of Hromadske Radio. “One woman is blind, she is 81, and she said she wants to support us financially — for her that's very important... She sent greetings to everyone. She knows us all by our voices and especially always waits for the 5:00 PM news bulletin.” Messages like these inspire the station’s tireless effort to maintain and expand broadcasting.

Like many markets, Ukraine was hit hard by the closure of USAID, which had supported independent, public interest media as a pillar of democracy. Some 333 outlets have shut down in the country over the past four years, lost to a combination of collapsing ad revenue and aid cuts. In 2024, the International Fund awarded flexible funding to Hromadske Radio to sustain its delivery of trustworthy news to audiences in Ukraine and the diaspora. The Fund's grant has helped Hromadske Radio expand its digital presence, build a coherent brand strategy, diversify its income and, most of all, keep broadcasting despite the challenging security situation.

"When a station like Hromadske Radio stays on air through bombardment and blackout, it's not just reporting the war, it's holding a society together.”

"When a station like Hromadske Radio stays on air through bombardment and blackout, it's not just reporting the war, it's holding a society together,” said Rita Rudusa, IFPIM’s Regional Director for Eastern Europe. “Independent media is one of the first things authoritarian forces try to destroy, and one of the last things the world remembers to fund. Our role is to make sure outlets like this can stay the course during the war, and survive beyond it."

Hromadske Radio’s experience is representative of the challenges facing Ukrainian news media more broadly. According to Reporters Without Borders (RSF) more than 175 Ukrainian and international journalists have been victims of Russian attacks in the four years since the invasion began. That figure includes 16 killed, at least 56 injured—mostly in drone strikes—and 26 detained. Beyond attacks on individuals, RSF has documented at least 25 attacks on news infrastructure, like those sustained by Hromadske Radio, including the bombing and occupation of broadcasting towers. In occupied regions, Russian forces routinely move to cut off Ukrainian programming and replace it with pro-Russia radio content and misleading narratives. In this context, direct support to independent outlets can be a gamechanger when it comes to ensuring the continued presence of a free and independent press.  

“We must keep the transmitters in frontline regions running: these are investments that determine whether or not people there hear verified information,” said Viktoriia Yermolaieva, Editor in Chief of Hromadske Radio. “In this context, core funding allows us to maintain our capacity to operate, keep the team together, invest in rapidly developing technologies, improve our format, increase the quantity and quality of content, pay for critically important infrastructure, and continue broadcasting where people urgently need it. This gives Hromadske Radio not just funding for an individual project, but stability—the ability to plan, develop, and set editorial priorities according to the needs of the audience and life in wartime conditions.”

By being able to stay and deliver, Hromadske Radio is now a trusted news source for roughly 580,000 weekly listeners. Their reach on YouTube and Facebook both has increased by ~65% since they became an IFPIM grantee, meaningful growth for an organization with mature social channels. In addition to reaching people on radio waves and digital channels, Hromadske Radio has started hosting in-person events designed to translate the subjects of their reporting into live dialogues. The events covered social topics like gender equality, LGBTQ+ rights, Ukrainian-Jewish history, and media accountability. The station has also invested heavily in making their website and programs accessible for those with disabilities—implementing AI powered voiceovers for all articles and alt text for images—and helping other newsrooms do the same. For this work, the station received an award for ‘Best Practices for Equality and Diversity in Ukrainian Newsrooms,’ in March 2026 from the National Council of Ukraine for Television and Radio Broadcasting, a national "Women in Media" NGO, and International Media Support.

Especially during a war, where information is contested as fiercely as territory, independent journalism is not a luxury. It is infrastructure, as vital as power lines or roads, and just as hard to rebuild once lost. Supporting outlets like Hromadske Radio is how democratic governments and others opposed to autocracy can ensure that news infrastructure remains where it is needed most, and that reliable facts and information can reach people in even the darkest conditions.

‍

item.title: A Deeper Look at How Indus Action Helps Strengthen India’s Social and Economic Safety Net
item.description:
How a model built on trust brings social and financial benefits within reach for more vulnerable families 

How do you support workers and their families in a country where there is no shared definition of “work”?  

Nine in 10 working citizens in India are employed in the informal sector—often in daily gigs that lack income stability. This intense job insecurity in a country with some 600 million people of working age is one of the challenges Indus Action sought to address. 

The organization, a 2026 Skoll Awardee, fills the gap between government intent and real-world impact. It helps millions of Indians understand, access, and claim benefits from more than 5,000 social protection programs the government offers, targeting workers, students, new mothers, and others experiencing life shocks.

India’s benefits programs are generous, but they’re also complex, difficult to understand, and require onerous application processes. As such, they’re functionally inaccessible for many of the people they are intended to support.

Indus Action’s technological, mobile-first solutions and community outreach are particularly welcome for the diverse population of informal workers who aren’t aware of the labor protections available to them. Even those who know they are eligible often don’t have the time, know-how, or flexibility in their daily schedules to carry out the average of 10 steps needed to claim benefits.

But the cost of not doing so is incredibly high:

By building the government’s capacity to deliver entitlement programs, strengthening community outreach, and harnessing technology to design and roll out citizen-centric solutions, Indus Action has connected 3.4 million citizens with their entitlements. This includes 1.8 million workers who received livelihood benefits.

On a macro level, Indus Action’s ability to help the government scale its intended labor protections for workers ultimately has the potential to create clearer pathways toward greater economic mobility for millions. The impact is particularly stark in the construction sector, which, as India’s second-largest industry, employs 71 million people and is projected to top 100 million by 2030.

Yet this sector is particularly vulnerable to economic shocks due to temporary work arrangements, informal relationships with employers, and frequent relocations to new job sites. These barriers make it difficult to demonstrate eligibility for existing welfare programs.

And with a growing Indian population that relies on functional infrastructure such as roads and airports, construction is vital to the country’s economic growth—highlighting that Indus Action’s support for this population is a positive force for greater economic stability overall.

In addition to workers, Indus Action helps families navigate what it calls “moments that matter,” such as the birth of a child, a period of unemployment, claiming a pension, or earning a scholarship. It has helped 949,842 students access school admissions or scholarships and more than 172,446 mothers access maternity health benefits. Together, these benefits help millions of people chart pathways out of poverty—lifting the entire economy.

What Makes the Model Successful

Founder and CEO Tarun Cherukuri emphasizes the importance of building two-way trust between citizens and government, including the last-mile community outreach workers responsible for registering individuals for benefits. His vision for Indus Action is to infuse greater relationship-building into a system that can often feel faceless.

“That’s our societal vision: this idea of relational state capacity,” he says, “where both sides—the citizen and the last-mile worker—are able to see each other’s humanity.”

Learn more about Indus Action’s impact on families.

The post A Deeper Look at How Indus Action Helps Strengthen India’s Social and Economic Safety Net appeared first on Skoll.org.

It has helped 949,842 students access school admissions or scholarships and more than 172,446 mothers access maternity health benefits. Together, these benefits help millions of people chart pathways out of poverty—lifting the entire economy.

What Makes the Model Successful

Founder and CEO Tarun Cherukuri emphasizes the importance of building two-way trust between citizens and government, including the last-mile community outreach workers responsible for registering individuals for benefits. His vision for Indus Action is to infuse greater relationship-building into a system that can often feel faceless.

“That’s our societal vision: this idea of relational state capacity,” he says, “where both sides—the citizen and the last-mile worker—are able to see each other’s humanity.”

Learn more about Indus Action’s impact on families.

The post A Deeper Look at How Indus Action Helps Strengthen India’s Social and Economic Safety Net appeared first on Skoll.org.

item.title: Fundação Bissaya Barreto admite pedreiro/a
item.description:
A FUNDAÇÃO BISSAYA BARRETO PRETENDE RECRUTAR 1 PEDREIRO/A

DADOS PESSOAIS E PRIVACIDADE: Para se candidatar, deve tomar conhecimento da política de tratamento de dados e privacidade desta instituição, disponível em http://www.fbb.pt/politica-de-privacidade-e-tratamento-de-dados/. Ao submeter as suas informações está a tomar conhecimento e a aceitar esses termos.

A Fundação Bissaya Barreto promove o direito à igualdade no acesso a emprego e no trabalho, em cumprimento do art.º 24º do Código do Trabalho (Lei n.º 7/2009, de 12 de fevereiro), no que diz respeito a critérios de seleção e a condições de contratação.

Tarefas

Competirá, nomeadamente, ao(à) trabalhador(a) a recrutar:

– Preparar argamassas;

– Executar alvenarias por assentamento de tijolo, pedra e/ou blocos de cimento;

– Executar rebocos, betonilhas e outros trabalhos similares e complementares;

– Executar esboços, estuques e lambris, bem como os respetivos acabamentos;

– Aplicar revestimentos de gesso cartonado (pladur), com os respetivos acabamentos;

– Pintar paredes, tetos, janelas e portas de madeira;

– Assentar pisos e azulejos;

– Assentar manilhas, tubos ou cantarias;

– Assentar vidros, com os respetivos trabalhos complementares;

– Outros trabalhos não específicos, enquadráveis no seu nível de qualificação.

Remuneração mensal

· 947,00 € (valor ilíquido)

· Subsídio de alimentação ou fornecimento de refeição

Requisitos de candidatura e competências valorizadas

· Carta de condução de viatura ligeira (requisito obrigatório)

· Veículo próprio (requisito obrigatório)

· Domínio da língua portuguesa

· Experiência mínima de cinco anos nas funções a que se candidata

· Escolaridade mínima obrigatória

· Robustez física para a função a que se candidata

· Gosto pelo trabalho em equipa

· Versatilidade

· Competências de carpintaria e de serralharia serão valorizadas

Tipo de contrato

Contrato de trabalho a termo

Formalização de candidaturas

Currículo profissional e académico, com indicação do lugar a que se candidata:

· Certificado de habilitações e comprovativos da experiência e formação profissional mencionadas no CV

Apresentação de candidaturas

· Via eletrónica: recrutamento@fbb.pt

Métodos de selecção

· Avaliação Curricular

· Entrevista profissional de seleção

· Prova prática

Local de trabalho

O(a) trabalhador(a) a recrutar será afeto(a) ao Serviço de Obras e Manutenção, para prestação de serviços no concelho de Coimbra, principalmente na zona de Bencanta e de Santa Clara;

Prazo limite de candidatura

30.09.2026

The post Fundação Bissaya Barreto admite pedreiro/a appeared first on Fundação Bissaya Barreto.

item.title: Fundação Bissaya Barreto pretende reforçar a equipa do Fundo Sociedade Civil / EEA Grants, com um/a Técnico/a de Comunicação
item.description:
Dados Pessoais e Privacidade

Para se candidatar, deve tomar conhecimento da política de tratamento de dados e privacidade desta instituição, disponível em https://www.fbb.pt/politica-de-privacidade-e-tratamento-de-dados-pessoais/

Ao submeter as suas informações está a tomar conhecimento e a aceitar esses termos.

A Fundação Bissaya Barreto promove o direito à igualdade no acesso a emprego e no trabalho, em cumprimento do art.º 24º do Código do Trabalho (Lei n.º 7/2009, de 12 de fevereiro), no que diz respeito a critérios de seleção e a condições de contratação.

FUNÇÕES

No âmbito desta função, será co-responsável por desenvolver e implementar a estratégia de comunicação do Programa Civil Society Fund – EEA Grants, em Portugal, assegurando a criação de conteúdos digitais para a divulgação eficaz das iniciativas do Programa e o reforço da sua visibilidade. Trabalhará em estreita articulação com a equipa do Programa e as respetivas equipas de comunicação dos parceiros do consórcio.

Criação e Gestão de Conteúdos:

· Desenvolver conteúdos de comunicação para diferentes plataformas e formatos digitais, incluindo redes sociais, website, newsletters, apresentações e materiais promocionais;

· Produzir e/ou coordenar a produção de conteúdos multimédia, como vídeos curtos, entrevistas, reportagens, fotografias, infografias e histórias de impacto;

· Acompanhar, in loco, as iniciativas dos projetos apoiados em Portugal Continental e Ilhas, para a criação de conteúdos multimédia;

· Redigir, editar e assegurar a qualidade de todos os materiais de comunicação do Programa, incluindo artigos, apresentações, relatórios e conteúdos promocionais sobre o Programa;

· Atualizar os conteúdos dos websites da Fundação e dos EEA Grants dedicados ao Programa;

· Transformar informação técnica em narrativas claras, humanas e envolventes, adaptadas a diferentes públicos.

Apoio à Comunicação Estratégica:

· Apoiar o desenvolvimento e implementação da estratégia de comunicação do Programa, em articulação com o consórcio e a equipa do Programa;

· Utilizar ferramentas de análise e métricas para avaliar o alcance, o impacto e os resultados das ações de comunicação, ajustando as estratégias quando necessário;

· Apoiar o planeamento e organização de eventos presenciais e online, como conferências, webinars, sessões de capacitação e workshops desenvolvidos pela equipa do Programa;

· Participar e representar o Programa em reuniões e eventos nacionais e/ou internacionais promovidos pelo financiador ou outras entidades, sempre que relevante.

REQUISITOS DE CANDIDATURA

· Licenciatura em Comunicação, Marketing, Produção audiovisual, Design ou áreas equivalentes;

· Experiência profissional mínima de 2 a 3 anos em funções similares;

· Competências técnicas em produção de vídeo, edição e pós-produção, motion graphics, webdesign ou outras áreas que potenciem a comunicação do Programa;

· Experiência em storytelling e comunicação de impacto;

· Conhecimento prático de ferramentas e plataformas de comunicação (redes sociais, CMS, ferramentas de analytics, etc.);

· Disponibilidade para deslocações para várias regiões do país, com eventuais deslocações ao estrangeiro;

· Excelentes competências de redação e domínio da língua portuguesa e inglesa;

· Conhecimento e/ou experiência nas áreas de intervenção do Programa (sociedade civil, da justiça social, dos direitos humanos) e do setor não lucrativo;

· Boa capacidade de comunicação, autonomia e espírito de equipa.

FORMALIZAÇÃO DE CANDIDATURAS

· Carta de motivação;

· Currículo profissional e académico, com foto.

APRESENTAÇÃO DE CANDIDATURAS Via eletrónica, enviando por e-mail os elementos solicitados para: recrutamento@fbb.pt

MÉTODOS DE SELEÇÃO

Avaliação curricular e entrevista profissional de seleção.

LOCAL DE TRABALHO

Bencanta – Coimbra.

TIPO DE VÍNCULO

Contrato de trabalho.

PRAZO LIMITE DE CANDIDATURA

13.09.2026

The post Fundação Bissaya Barreto pretende reforçar a equipa do Fundo Sociedade Civil / EEA Grants, com um/a Técnico/a de Comunicação appeared first on Fundação Bissaya Barreto.

item.title: Meet LOOKOUT News
item.description:
Meet LOOKOUT News, the US Southwest’s only nonprofit LGBTQ+ newsroom. Its mission is to deliver fearless journalism and community events that expand LGBTQ+ representation on the local news stage, while strengthening and engaging LGBTQ+ communities and their allies. LOOKOUT‘s ultimate vision is a queer experience liberated from injustice, with equal respect, rights, and opportunity for all people, backed by journalism that holds power accountable.

Founders Joseph Darius Jafaari and Jake Hylton started LOOKOUT in December 2022 because the data was clear: local news coverage of queer people and the issues affecting them was disappearing outside of election cycles and Pride month. When it did show up, it usually talked over the community’s voices, rather than including them. They wanted to change that.

It started as Jafaari’s monthly newsletter but has since grown into a full operation. LOOKOUT now publish a quarterly print magazine and three regular weekly newsletters, including their legislative tracker Eyes on the State, reaching a community of more than 15,000 readers. It also built the Glitterati, a volunteer street team that shows up at events across Arizona to get LOOKOUT directly into people’s hands.

In just its second year of eligibility, LOOKOUT has been racking up recognition, including a Business of the Year nomination from LION Publishers and four honors at the 2026 Association of Alternative Newsmedia Awards:

First Place – AAN Excellence in Journalism for Under the Badge, an investigative series by Celina Jiménez examining how law enforcement agencies across Arizona respond to violence targeting LGBTQ+ people.

First Place – LGBTQ+ Coverage for reporter Tori Gantz’s body of work exploring the intersection of queerness and far-right politics.

First Place – Newsletter for Eyes on the State, LOOKOUT‘s legislative newsletter by Tori Gantz tracking hundreds of bills affecting LGBTQ+ Arizonans during the legislative session.

Third Place – LGBTQ+ Coverage for Escaping Arizona, a reported series by Joseph Darius Jaafari and Ellie Samsal exploring why LGBTQ+ Arizonans are leaving the state amid an increasingly hostile political climate.

Founder and Editor-in-Chief Joseph Darius Jaafari also received the Spirit of AAN Award for his leadership in the field. 

Beyond reporting, the organization’s flagship programs like Summer of Solutions and Reporting as Resistance train community members in journalism fundamentals, empowering those closest to the issues to tell their own stories. The Spring 2026 cohort covered stories ranging from a crepe shop doubling as a safe haven for activists to frontline medics tending to elderly protesters in the summer heat. 

In exciting news, LOOKOUT officially expanded into Colorado in June after a feasibility study and months of listening sessions across the region. Thinking intentionally about building roots in the community, LOOKOUT started with a launch event in Denver for local partners, funders, and publishers. It also tabled at Denver Pride, where more than 400 people signed up to receive the newsletter. LOOKOUT plans to continue expanding its coverage to Utah, New Mexico, and Nevada, hiring local talent that are already embedded in each community.

We invite you to follow along with their work and read some of their recent articles:

  • A Trans Woman Detained in a Deadly Arizona Detention Center Refuses to be Silent
  • They Followed the Rules. Now They’re Being Targeted for Deportation.
  • Dozens of Arizona Officials Call for Humanitarian Release of Phoenix Queer Woman Held by ICE
  • LGBTQ+ outlet LOOKOUT aims to expand throughout the Southwest, and beyond 

The post Meet LOOKOUT News appeared first on The Reva and David Logan Foundation.

First Place – LGBTQ+ Coverage for reporter Tori Gantz’s body of work exploring the intersection of queerness and far-right politics.

First Place – Newsletter for Eyes on the State, LOOKOUT‘s legislative newsletter by Tori Gantz tracking hundreds of bills affecting LGBTQ+ Arizonans during the legislative session.

Third Place – LGBTQ+ Coverage for Escaping Arizona, a reported series by Joseph Darius Jaafari and Ellie Samsal exploring why LGBTQ+ Arizonans are leaving the state amid an increasingly hostile political climate.

Founder and Editor-in-Chief Joseph Darius Jaafari also received the Spirit of AAN Award for his leadership in the field. 

Beyond reporting, the organization’s flagship programs like Summer of Solutions and Reporting as Resistance train community members in journalism fundamentals, empowering those closest to the issues to tell their own stories. The Spring 2026 cohort covered stories ranging from a crepe shop doubling as a safe haven for activists to frontline medics tending to elderly protesters in the summer heat. 

In exciting news, LOOKOUT officially expanded into Colorado in June after a feasibility study and months of listening sessions across the region. Thinking intentionally about building roots in the community, LOOKOUT started with a launch event in Denver for local partners, funders, and publishers. It also tabled at Denver Pride, where more than 400 people signed up to receive the newsletter. LOOKOUT plans to continue expanding its coverage to Utah, New Mexico, and Nevada, hiring local talent that are already embedded in each community.

We invite you to follow along with their work and read some of their recent articles:

  • A Trans Woman Detained in a Deadly Arizona Detention Center Refuses to be Silent
  • They Followed the Rules. Now They’re Being Targeted for Deportation.
  • Dozens of Arizona Officials Call for Humanitarian Release of Phoenix Queer Woman Held by ICE
  • LGBTQ+ outlet LOOKOUT aims to expand throughout the Southwest, and beyond 

The post Meet LOOKOUT News appeared first on The Reva and David Logan Foundation.

item.title: A Deeper Look Inside ChildLife Foundation’s Life-Saving Model
item.description:
Here’s how ChildLife Foundation tackles child mortality in Pakistan while championing female physicians

In Pakistan, where families are plagued by one of the highest under-five mortality rates in the world, one organization asked a powerful question: How many of the 1,000 children who die every day could we save by rethinking basic health care infrastructure?

To answer it, 2026 Skoll Awardee ChildLife Foundation looked at the structures and systems already in place throughout the country and devised a way to transform them without building new facilities from scratch.

Through an innovative public-private partnership, ChildLife rehabilitates and manages 14 pediatric emergency rooms within public hospitals and links an additional 300 district facilities to pediatric specialists located in major cities through a telemedicine network. Through this model, it reaches 90 percent of the population and has achieved a tenfold reduction in mortality among critically ill children in the emergency rooms ChildLife manages.

For CEO Ahson Rabbani, the lightbulb moment—the one that led to the focus on improving the quality of care available in every corner of the country, not just urban centers—came from a devastating encounter with a woman facing an impossible choice:

What Makes the Model Successful

In addition to ChildLife’s 450 clinical staff with expertise in emergency medicine, the organization leans on its business-minded professionals, who together collaboratively design and implement processes that transform complex health care systems into finely tuned operations capable of saving lives. For Rabbani, who brings engineering and management training, the success of these emergency rooms comes down to embedding best practices into every facility, every step of the way. “It’s all about processes,” he says.  

Like many social entrepreneurs, ChildLife Foundation is exploring how to continue infusing new technologies throughout its model to increase access to and quality of services. In addition to its telemedicine network, the organization harnesses artificial intelligence to improve clinical decision-making, make more efficient use of doctors’ time, and ensure consistency for all patients.

The impact on children is clear: pediatric mortality in ChildLife-managed ERs dropped to 1.2 percent, comparable to Pakistan’s top private hospitals.

What’s less obvious is the profound impact on the health care workforce. With modernized facilities and equipment, best-in-class training and processes, and a sustainable funding stream from philanthropy and government partnerships, physicians are better able to deliver on their mission to save lives.

And for female clinicians especially, ChildLife’s model opens doors to lasting economic opportunity and independence. Although women comprise the vast majority of medical graduates in Pakistan—up to 80 percent—about half either did not enter the practice or left after a short time. The primary culprit is structural barriers, including workplace safety risks, access challenges, cultural norms, and familial restrictions.

ChildLife’s telemedicine model addresses these obstacles, enabling highly trained female clinicians to pursue stable, safe employment that is both professionally challenging and personally meaningful, without having to commute long distances or choose between work and family. As a result, women hold more than half of the organization’s managerial positions and make up nearly three-fourths of its total workforce.

The organization’s gender-inclusive policies and approach earned the designation of Best Place to Work for Women in Pakistan in 2025 by the Pakistan Society of Human Resource Management. And, by leveraging an untapped pool of local talent to supplement the care available only in urban areas, ChildLife ensures larger swaths of the rural population can access specialized medical expertise. 

Learn more here about ChildLife’s impact on Pakistani communities.

The post A Deeper Look Inside ChildLife Foundation’s Life-Saving Model appeared first on Skoll.org.

item.title: From tradition to transformation in Mexico: taking time for reflection, conversation, and healing
item.description:
From neighbourhood bakeries to community networks, women-led organisations across Mexico are creating spaces where women and girls affected by violence can heal, connect, and thrive. Through emotional support, legal assistance, economic empowerment, and collective care, they are helping them recover, reclaim their autonomy, and build new futures.

item.title: Successes, Failures, and Lessons Learned
item.description:
Stephen Heintz at the United Nations in 2024.

The following first appeared in Inside Philanthropy. The opinions expressed are those of the author and do not necessarily represent the views of the Rockefeller Brothers Fund.

[...]

By most accounts, Heintz has been one of the sector’s most successful top executives. But he is also keenly aware of those areas where he didn’t succeed — or, in some cases, totally failed. In a recent interview, we talked through both his successes and his failures, along with the lessons he’s learned along the way.

At the top of Heintz’s list of successes is modernizing the foundation, which was created in 1940 by the five sons of John D. Rockefeller Jr. and now has assets of $1.4 billion. When he took over, it was widely respected, but had not innovated much.

“Walking into the RBF in 2001 was like finding myself in a new home for me that was a beautiful old house, but discovering that it needed new wiring and new plumbing, and tearing down some of the walls to open up spaces,” Heintz said. It was “this venerable and wonderful institution,” he said, but “was trying to do too many things in too many places in the world with too little money to really have significant impact.”

Heintz revamped the RBF, improving its management systems and organizing grantmaking around a smaller number of themes and “pivotal places.”

Read more in Inside Philanthropy.

item.title: NewsInternational Fund Appoints Amélie Baudot as New Chief Executive OfficerThe Board of the International Fund for Public Interest Media has appointed Amélie Baudot, currently Deputy CEO, as the new Chief Executive Officer of IFPIM, following Nishant Lalwani’s decision to step down after four years in the role.
item.description:
Press Releases

Paris, 17 August: The Board of the International Fund for Public Interest Media has appointed Amélie Baudot, currently Deputy CEO, as the new Chief Executive Officer of the Fund, following Nishant Lalwani’s decision to step down after four years in the role. Mr Lalwani will continue to support the International Fund in a non-executive capacity. Ms Baudot will take up her position as CEO as of October 1st.

A founding member of the International Fund's leadership team, Amélie Baudot has been instrumental in shaping its vision and spearheading its establishment as an international organization in France — a status that has proven to be transformative for the International Fund. With over a decade of experience managing global, multi-donor impact funds, Amélie has built a reputation for confronting and solving complex challenges faced by societies. Before joining IFPIM, she was the Chief Strategy and Legal Officer of the Global Innovation Fund, a non-profit impact-first investment fund where Amélie pioneered their strategy to diversify sources of funding and create a new model for blended finance.

“We are thrilled that Amélie Baudot is taking on the role as CEO. She brings deep institutional knowledge of IFPIM, real ambition for what comes next, and a proven ability to build both the partnerships and the people needed to get there”, said Mark Thompson, Co-chair of the International Fund Board. “As a Board, we see this as an opportunity to build on what has already been accomplished and we’re excited about moving the Fund’s work forward under Amélie’s leadership, into a bolder chapter for independent journalism and public interest information around the world”. 

As the International Fund’s co-founder in 2019 and CEO since August 2022, Nishant Lalwani has been a driving force behind IFPIM, from commissioning the feasibility study that lead to the Fund’s inception, to building a coalition of donors and partners committed to independent media at precisely the moment much of the world was walking away from it.

“Under Nishant’s leadership, the Fund has grown from a novel idea into a first-of-its-kind International Organization that has supported over 150 media outlets around the world,” said Maria Ressa, IFPIM Board Co-chair.  “At a time when journalists in the Global South are being silenced, sued, and left desperately short of funding, Nishant has built an institution that stands behind them. The Board is enormously thankful to him for the strong foundation he has put in place at IFPIM, and is grateful that he will stay involved with the Fund for the years to come.”

“Quality journalism is the connective tissue of communities and societies and we have a duty to ensure its future for all,” said Amelie Baudot. “Over the past four years, IFPIM and partners have worked to ensure that people have access to trusted and accurate information for the simple and complex choices we make in our every day lives. As CEO, I will work alongside our exceptional partners, this talented team and our dedicated Board and Council, to ensure that the International Fund continues to deliver on this vital mission.” 

Over the next several months, Mr Lalwani and Ms Baudot will be working closely with the Board and Executive Team to manage the transition. IFPIM’s commitments to its partners, donors and the journalists it supports remain unchanged.

item.title: Droom ineens een stuk dichterbij Winnaarsverhalen 18 augustus 2026 Een dak dat opgeknapt moet worden én een grote droom in Frankrijk. Willemijn en Sander weten wel raad met hun prijs van tien jaar lang € 25.000,-. Lees meer
item.description:
"Droom ineens een stuk dichterbij": Willemijn en Sander uit Tilburg winnen tien jaar lang € 25.000, -. Het stel uit Tilburg werkt allebei in de horeca en droomt al heel lang van een eigen bed & breakfast in Frankrijk. Dan belt Gaston aan, met een gouden envelop

dinsdag 18 augustus 2026 - Winnaarsverhalen

Gaston en zijn team rijden Tilburg binnen, richting de Plus-winnaars. Hij belt aan bij Willemijn en Sander en loopt met ze mee naar de tuin. Daar haalt hij de cheque uit de envelop. Zodra het stel doorheeft wat ze zien staan, slaan ze allebei hun handen voor hun mond. Tien jaar lang € 25.000,- per jaar.

"Perfect moment"

"Je verwacht het niet", zegt een zichtbaar zenuwachtige Willemijn. En dat klopt: de Plus prijs viel dit keer op hun postcode. Willemijn en Sander werken allebei in de horeca en kunnen hun geluk nauwelijks op. "De prijs komt op een perfect moment. Onze woning is toe aan een flinke opknapbeurt. Het dak moet worden gerenoveerd en geschilderd. Met deze geldprijs kunnen wij deze plannen gaan uitvoeren."

Een droom in een Frans wijngebied

Maar daar blijft het niet bij. Want Willemijn en Sander koesteren al jaren een grotere wens. "We hebben al heel lang de droom om ooit een huis te kopen in een Frans wijngebied en daar een eigen bed & breakfast te beginnen. Met deze prijs lijkt die langgekoesterde wens ineens een stuk dichterbij."

As CEO, I will work alongside our exceptional partners, this brilliant team and our dedicated Board and Council, to ensure that the International Fund continues to deliver on this vital mission.”

item.content:encoded:
Press Releases

Paris, 17 August: The Board of the International Fund for Public Interest Media has appointed Amélie Baudot, currently Deputy CEO, as the new Chief Executive Officer of the Fund, following Nishant Lalwani’s decision to step down after four years in the role. Mr Lalwani will continue to support the International Fund in a non-executive capacity. Ms Baudot will take up her position as CEO as of October 1st.

A founding member of the International Fund's leadership team, Amélie Baudot has been instrumental in shaping its vision and spearheading its establishment as an international organization in France — a status that has proven to be transformative for the International Fund. With over a decade of experience managing global, multi-donor impact funds, Amélie has built a reputation for confronting and solving complex challenges faced by societies. Before joining IFPIM, she was the Chief Strategy and Legal Officer of the Global Innovation Fund, a non-profit impact-first investment fund where Amélie pioneered their strategy to diversify sources of funding and create a new model for blended finance.

“We are thrilled that Amélie Baudot is taking on the role as CEO. She brings deep institutional knowledge of IFPIM, real ambition for what comes next, and a proven ability to build both the partnerships and the people needed to get there”, said Mark Thompson, Co-chair of the International Fund Board. “As a Board, we see this as an opportunity to build on what has already been accomplished and we’re excited about moving the Fund’s work forward under Amélie’s leadership, into a bolder chapter for independent journalism and public interest information around the world”. 

As the International Fund’s co-founder in 2019 and CEO since August 2022, Nishant Lalwani has been a driving force behind IFPIM, from commissioning the feasibility study that lead to the Fund’s inception, to building a coalition of donors and partners committed to independent media at precisely the moment much of the world was walking away from it.

“Under Nishant’s leadership, the Fund has grown from a novel idea into a first-of-its-kind International Organization that has supported over 150 media outlets around the world,” said Maria Ressa, IFPIM Board Co-chair.  “At a time when journalists in the Global South are being silenced, sued, and left desperately short of funding, Nishant has built an institution that stands behind them. The Board is enormously thankful to him for the strong foundation he has put in place at IFPIM, and is grateful that he will stay involved with the Fund for the years to come.”

“Quality journalism is the connective tissue of communities and societies and we have a duty to ensure its future for all,” said Amelie Baudot. “Over the past four years, IFPIM and partners have worked to ensure that people have access to trusted and accurate information for the simple and complex choices we make in our every day lives. As CEO, I will work alongside our exceptional partners, this brilliant team and our dedicated Board and Council, to ensure that the International Fund continues to deliver on this vital mission.” 

Over the next several months, Mr Lalwani and Ms Baudot will be working closely with the Board and Executive Team to manage the transition. IFPIM’s commitments to its partners, donors and the journalists it supports remain unchanged.

item.title: Irma en Eric uit Bakel genieten volop van hun nieuwe Volkswagen ID. Buzz Winnaarsverhalen Premium 17 augustus 2026 Een aantal maanden geleden stond Caroline Tensen met een bijzondere verrassing voor de deur bij Irma en Eric uit Bakel. Het stel viel in de prijzen met Premium en won een gloednieuwe Volkswagen ID. Buzz. Inmiddels hebben ze de sleutels in ontvangst genomen en kunnen ze volop genieten van hun nieuwe auto. Lees meer
item.description:
Een aantal maanden geleden stond Caroline Tensen met een bijzondere verrassing voor de deur bij Irma en Eric uit Bakel. Het stel viel in de prijzen met Premium en won een gloednieuwe Volkswagen ID. Buzz. Inmiddels hebben ze de sleutels in ontvangst genomen en kunnen ze volop genieten van hun nieuwe auto.

maandag 17 augustus 2026 — Winnaarsverhalen, Premium

“We zijn er heel erg blij mee! Hij rijdt als een grootvorst”, vertelt Eric enthousiast. Om hun prijs op te halen, reisden Irma en Eric speciaal met de trein naar Amsterdam. Vanaf daar reden ze in hun nieuwe Volkswagen terug naar Bakel.


En de ID. Buzz heeft inmiddels al de nodige kilometers gemaakt. “We zijn er al mee naar Amersfoort en Zoetermeer geweest. Heerlijk een rondje toeren om de auto goed te leren kennen.”

Een verrassing op vrijdag de dertiende

Ook de feestelijke uitreiking aan huis staat het stel nog goed bij. “Het was echt een heel leuke verrassing. We hebben na afloop nog gezellig gekletst en het team Brabantse worstenbroodjes mee naar huis gegeven.”


Dat Caroline juist op vrijdag de dertiende voor de deur stond, maakt het verhaal voor Eric extra bijzonder. “Toen was vrijdag de dertiende opeens geen ongeluksdag meer!”


Na het goede nieuws belden Irma en Eric meteen hun dochters. Daarna werd er natuurlijk een borreltje gedronken om de prijs te vieren. Het nieuws ging vervolgens snel rond. “We waren een paar dagen even bekende Bakelaars”, lacht Eric.


Ook vanuit de buurt kwamen veel enthousiaste reacties. “We hebben een onwijs meelevende buurt, dus iedereen reageerde blij en enthousiast.”


Met de sleutels op zak en de eerste mooie ritten achter de rug, kunnen Irma en Eric voorlopig nog heerlijk genieten van hun bijzondere prijs.

item.title: EU Support to Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood Partners on Migration and Forced Displacement
item.description:
Migration and forced displacement are global phenomena. The EU works with third countries and international partners to better manage migration and mobility along different migratory routes. This cooperation helps address the challenges and harness the opportunities linked to international migration while also promoting safe and legal alternatives to irregular migration. For the Directorate-General for Enlargement and the Eastern Neighbourhood (DG ENEST), migration is both a strategic priority and a key area of the EU’s engagement in its immediate neighbourhood.

All EU actions and external partnerships are guided by international law and the protection of fundamental rights. These include the protection of vulnerable migrants, asylum seekers and refugees. The EU is committed to addressing the root causes of irregular migration and combating smuggling of migrants and trafficking in human beings. The EU also supports voluntary returns and sustainable reintegration of returnees in their countries of origin and the returns of irregularly staying migrants to their countries of origin. EU action and partnerships also cover legal migration and labour mobility.

The EU follows a whole-of-route approach in its cooperation with countries of origin and transit along the main migratory routes. In addition, it also relies on cooperation with relevant EU agencies, including the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), the EU Asylum Agency (EUAA), and Europol, as well as with the UN and other international partners.

The external dimension of EU migration policy is based on a comprehensive approach to migration and asylum. This approach is guided by the Conclusions of the European Council, the five-year European Asylum and Migration Management Strategy 2026-2031 and the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum. The Pact underlines that migration should not be addressed in isolation and should form part of comprehensive, balanced, tailor-made and mutually beneficial partnerships with countries of origin and transit. These partnerships should generate mutual benefits in areas such as the economy, development, stability and security, education, skills, and people-to-people contacts. 

In line with this approach, and in full coordination with EU Member States as Team Europe, the EU is strengthening its partnerships along migratory routes, notably through regional EU Action Plans.

Accession and Policy Alignment

For countries on the path to EU membership, alignment under Chapter 24 (Justice, Freedom, and Security) is a core component of the accession framework and process. It requires candidate countries to progressively align their national legislation, visa policies, and asylum systems with the EU legislation, including with the Pact on Migration and Asylum. Important topics such as legal migration, combating irregular entry and smuggling, asylum procedures, return policies, and visa policy harmonization are covered within this framework.

Western Balkans

The Western Balkans remains a top strategic priority for the EU, with efforts aimed at securing borders and dismantling criminal smuggling networks. Work is carried out through strong and continuous cooperation with the region in line with the regional EU Action Plan for the Western Balkans. A key focus of this partnership is supporting partners in aligning  their national visa policies with the EU. This contributes to preventing irregular migration and maintaining the well-functioning visa-free travel regime between the region and the EU.

As part of the accession process, the EU also provides substantial financial and technical assistance to strengthen national asylum registration, protection, and reception capacities in close cooperation with the EUAA. Active status agreements with Frontex reinforce these efforts by allowing European Border and Coast Guard to participate in joint operations alongside national authorities of partner countries.

Türkiye

The EU-Turkey Statement provides the overall framework for migration cooperation, reinforced by the EU Action Plan for the Eastern Mediterranean Route. The EU remains committed to assisting Türkiye and host communities through a comprehensive approach:

  • Migration Management Assistance: Joint work focuses on preventing irregular departures, combatting human smuggling networks, and strengthening national border management, asylum, and reception capacities in line with international standards.
  • Refugee Support: Since 2011, the EU has provided €12 billion to ensure the basic needs of refugees and host communities are met. This funding provides sustained humanitarian assistance, healthcare, education, municipal infrastructure, and socio-economic support.

Eastern Partnership

In the Eastern Partnership region, EU cooperation focuses on securing borders, managing displacement, and facilitating safe legal mobility. For candidate countries, this work also directly supports their progressive alignment with EU legislation and standards.

The EU continues to sustain standard visa facilitation and readmission agreements across the wider region. In cooperation with partner countries and Frontex, the EU promotes secure border management that fully respects fundamental rights and international standards, while facilitating legal and mutually beneficial mobility.

Ukraine

Following Russia’s full-scale invasion and the resulting displacement crisis, the EU has prioritized protection and integration through the Temporary Protection Directive. Alongside these humanitarian measures, EU assistance supports stabilisation efforts, rule of law reforms, capacity building and other reforms linked to the EU accession process. Migration, asylum, support to Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and Integrated Border Management (IBM) play a central role in this approach, helping Ukraine manage displacement during the conflict.

Moldova

The EU provides dedicated funding to enhance the operational capacities, training, and equipment of national authorities, including Moldova’s police, border guards, and customs services. The EU also supports Moldova’s targeted efforts to combat and prevent organised crime and accelerate the digitalization of operations and training. Together, these measures help align Moldova’s border and migration management with EU standards and practices, bringing the country forward on its EU path.

Armenia

Under the Resilience and Growth Plan for Armenia, the EU delivers targeted support for migration-related reforms in the country. This funding focuses on upgrading border and migration management systems and helping Armenia meet the criteria required for its Visa Liberalisation goals.

item.title: Promoting education and skills
item.description:
Education on centre stage

The development of education and skills in the EU’s neighbouring partner countries and improved student and academic mobility is among the key areas of our EU support. A strong and educated human capital is a crucial factor in the enlargement process but also for  - building a common space of stability and prosperity between the EU and its neighbours, fostering social and economic development and accomplishing democratic transition processes in partner countries.

Erasmus+ programme is one of the key initiatives for EU cooperation  in education, training, youth and sport.  It is the main policy instrument in support of the European Education Area and the Union of Skills. At the same time the ERASMUS+ programme is an important initiative for the gradual integration and association of the enlargement partners to the EU policies in these fields.

Three ENEST countries are already fully associated to the programme – Türkiye, North-Macedonia and Serbia – meaning they can fully take part in all actions of the Erasmus+ Programme. The budget dedicated to the four non-associated Western Balkan partners for 2021-2027 is €362 million and for the Eastern Neighbourhood for more than €302 million and it includes four main actions:

  • Key Action 1 – Mobility of individuals:  Opportunities for pupils, students, adult learners, trainees and young people, as well as for professors, teachers, trainers, educators, youth workers, sport staff, staff of education institutions and civil society organisations to undertake a learning and/or professional experience in another country.
  • Key Action 2 - Cooperation among organisations and institutions: capacity building, institutional reform and related student and staff mobility.
  • Key Action 3 - Support to policy development and cooperation: policy support and policy dialogue, including project/information offices and promotional activities in ENP partner countries
  • Jean Monnet actions

Overview of support to higher education in 2021-2027

International Credit Mobility 

Short-term mobility for students and staff allows students to study at a foreign university for 2-12 months and obtain credits which are then recognised at the sending institution as part of their degree. In addition, there is a possibility to apply for a grant for staff mobility for 6-50 days.

Since 2022, over 30 230 people have participated in the mobility schemes that Erasmus+ programme provides, allowing for exchanges and mobility between the non-associated Western Balkans partners and EU countries, and 29 681 between the Eastern Neighbourhood and EU countries.

Capacity Building in Higher Education

Capacity Building projects in Higher Education are 2 to 3 year-long projects implemented by multilateral partnerships of Higher Education institutions from both programme countries and non-associated countries with the aim of modernising higher education institutions and systems. These projects contribute to curriculum development activities, modernisation of governance and management of higher education institutions and systems and strengthening relations between higher education and the wider economic and social environment.

Since 2022, 455 instances of participation by institutions from the non-associated Western Balkans partners in 66 different projects selected to benefit higher education, and 573 instances of participation by institutions from Neighbourhood East in 81 projects selected to benefit higher education in this region.

Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters

The Erasmus Mundus Joint master’s degrees are full-degree scholarships to Master students from around the world covering tuition, travel, and a living allowance. The programmes last from one to two years during which, students study in at least two different European countries. Upon graduation, they are awarded a joint or a double degree, or multiple degrees.

The EU funds additional scholarships for students from the non-associated Western Balkans partners . Institutions from the Western Balkan and Eastern Neighbourhood countries can also deliver these programmes.

Since 2021, 3 organisations from the non-associated Western Balkans partners countries have been involved as full partners of the Erasmus Mundus programmes and 200 scholarships have been granted for the nationals of the non-associated Western Balkans countries.

There have been 24 instances of Neighbourhood East organisations involved (partner or associate) in Erasmus Mundus programmes, 3 of them as full partners, and 427 scholarships have been granted for nationals of Neighbourhood East countries.

Jean Monnet Activities

Jean Monnet activities aim to develop EU studies worldwide. Modules, Chairs and Centres of Excellence promote excellence in teaching and research on the European integration process at higher education level. The programme also supports policy debate with the academic world through networks.

Since 2021, 55 projects have been managed by higher education institutions from the 4 Western Balkans partners. There are currently one Jean Monnet Network where an HEI from the Western Balkans, i.e. Bosnia and Herzegovina) is participating.

303 projects have been managed by HEIs from Neighbourhood East, with Ukraine leading the chart at 254 projects. As for now there are two Jean Monnet Networks where the HEIs from the Neighbourhood East (namely Ukraine) are participating.

European Universities Initiative (EUI)

The European Universities Initiative is a key flagship initiative in the field of higher education. 65 European Universities alliances are part of this initiative funded by Erasmus+, gathering over 570 higher education institutions from 35 countries. European Universities alliances are transnational alliances of higher education institutions developing long-term structural, strategic and sustainable cooperation, aiming to improve their international competitiveness, while promoting European values and identity.

Since 2023, as part of the Enhanced partnership within the region, higher education institutions from the four non-associated Western Balkan partners can participate in the EUI as full partners. This allows them to reinforce cooperation with the EU’s higher education systems, while strengthening their attractiveness and learning from peers. Their students and staff members can benefit from increased learning and work opportunities. As a result of this opening up of the EUI, 8 higher education institutions from Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro are currently involved as full partners in seven European Universities alliances.

For more details, check out the regional and country factsheets ENEST partners under the international dimension and for  associated countries.

item.title: From craft to community: building sustainable futures through hand crafts
item.description:
For artisans, craft is more than a livelihood. Nest helps entrepreneurs in the US grow thriving businesses and supports crafters across five continents through training, resources, and markets. By strengthening livelihoods, this helps sustain communities and keep cultural traditions flourishing.

The post From craft to community: building sustainable futures through hand crafts appeared first on Oak Foundation.

item.title: Zomerpret voor iedereen Goede doelen 14 augustus 2026 Voor veel kinderen betekent de zomervakantie tijd voor plezier, avontuur en mooie herinneringen. Maar voor kinderen in gezinnen met weinig geld, ziet de zomervakantie er heel anders uit. Lees meer
item.description:
Voor veel kinderen betekent de zomervakantie tijd voor plezier, avontuur en mooie herinneringen. Maar voor kinderen in gezinnen met weinig geld, ziet de zomervakantie er heel anders uit. Geen geld voor speelgoed, geen dagjes uit, geen vriendjes om mee te spelen. Daarom organiseert Kinderhulp ieder jaar Actie Zomerpret. 

vrijdag 14 augustus 2026 - Goede doelen

Zomerpretpakket

Dankzij een Zomerpretpakket kunnen duizenden kinderen deze zomer toch iets leuks beleven. In het pakket zitten onder meer vouchers voor een dagje uit, treinkaartjes, een cadeaukaart voor iets lekkers én cadeaus zoals een boek, spelletjes of speelgoed. Zo ontstaat er ruimte voor ontspanning, plezier en vooral tijd samen. 
 

Moeder Carolien en zoontje Joa

Moeder Carolien zag wat het pakket voor haar zoontje Joa betekende. "Joa was superblij met de LEGO en het leesboek dat erin zat. Ook zaten er spelletjes in en konden we samen een dagje uit. Dat maakte hem zo intens gelukkig." Juist die kleine momenten maken een groot verschil. Even onbezorgd spelen, eropuit gaan en herinneringen maken die nog lang blijven.

Een zomer waarin ieder kind mee kan doen

Directeur bestuurder Bernique Tool ziet ieder jaar hoeveel dit betekent. "Met de steun van onder andere de Postcode Loterij kunnen we al jaren kinderen helpen met een Zomerpretpakket. Deze zomer maar liefst 7.500 kinderen en jongeren! Zo kunnen ook zij eropuit en herinneringen maken. Geen luxe, maar gewoon een spel, wat ontspanning en een zomer om op terug te kijken. Dat geeft kinderen het gevoel dat ze erbij horen, gezien worden en ook mogen dromen." 

Samen maken we het verschil

Dankzij alle deelnemers kan de Postcode Loterij organisaties als Kinderhulp steunen. Zo krijgen duizenden kinderen de kans om mooie zomerherinneringen te maken.
item.content:encoded:
Voor veel kinderen betekent de zomervakantie tijd voor plezier, avontuur en mooie herinneringen. Maar voor kinderen in gezinnen met weinig geld, ziet de zomervakantie er heel anders uit. Geen geld voor speelgoed, geen dagjes uit, geen vriendjes om mee te spelen. Daarom organiseert Kinderhulp ieder jaar Actie Zomerpret. 

vrijdag 14 augustus 2026 - Goede doelen

Zomerpretpakket

Dankzij een Zomerpretpakket kunnen duizenden kinderen deze zomer toch iets leuks beleven. In het pakket zitten onder meer vouchers voor een dagje uit, treinkaartjes, een cadeaukaart voor iets lekkers én cadeaus zoals een boek, spelletjes of speelgoed. item.title: Een lammetje, een verjaardag en een miljoen Winnaarsverhalen 14 augustus 2026 Dit keer reist Gaston en zijn team af naar Breedenbroek, helemaal bij de Duitse grens. Op postcode 7084 AK is de SuperPostcodeprijs van € 1 MILJOEN gevallen. Lees meer
item.description:
Dit keer reist Gaston en zijn team af naar Breedenbroek, helemaal bij de Duitse grens. Op postcode 7084 AK is de SuperPostcodeprijs van € 1 MILJOEN gevallen.

vrijdag 14 augustus 2026 - Winnaarsverhalen

Een eigen huis

Lisa woont inmiddels in Arnhem, maar speelt nog mee op het adres van haar ouders. Als ze het bedrag op haar cheque ziet, slaat ze een hand voor haar mond. "Ik wil een eigen huis kopen, ik huur nu nog. En op vakantie, het liefst een wereldreis." Vader Peter kijkt trots toe: "Het is haar zo gegund!"

Woning splitsen

Gaston en zijn team vinden Rik pas na goed zoeken, tussen een paard, haar veulen en lammetje Bram, die hij zelf met de fles heeft grootgebracht. Rik heeft 4 kinderen. Als hij zijn prijs ziet, wordt het even stil. Maar na een korte stilte deelt hij zijn plan: "Ik wil de woning splitsen, zodat de kinderen er kunnen wonen."

Kleine straatjes maken ook kans

Ook bij Jutta en Gerrie klopt het hart in de keel. "Ik sta helemaal te trillen", zegt Jutta vlak voordat de cheque opengaat. Het stel droomt van een carport. "We wonen in een gebied met veel vogels die de auto onderpoepen." En een nieuw bankstel mag ook wel. "De rest laat ik aan Gerrie over", lacht ze. “Geef de hoop niet op! Wij dachten ook dat hij nooit in een klein straatje zou vallen zoals hier.”

Verjaardagsfeest met een feestelijke onderbreking

Annie zit samen met haar 2 zussen en zwager buiten om de verjaardag van één van de zussen te vieren. Wat ze met haar prijs wil doen? "Misschien iets aan het huis, en delen met familie."

item.title: Warm zomerweer op komst? Zoek de verkoeling op in de natuur Goede doelen 13 augustus 2026 Een wandeling door een schaduwrijk bos. Een route langs het water. Of een fietstocht met een frisse zeebries. In de natuur is het heerlijk genieten, ook op warme dagen. Lees meer
item.description:
Een wandeling door een schaduwrijk bos. Een route langs het water. Of een fietstocht met een frisse zeebries. In de natuur is het heerlijk genieten, ook op warme dagen. Dankzij onze deelnemers beschermen partners zoals LandschappenNL bijzondere natuurgebieden. En houden ze deze toegankelijk voor iedereen. Hier delen zij hun tips voor fijne wandelroutes. 

donderdag 13 augustus 2026 - Goede doelen

Drenthe | Spaarbankbos paaltjesroute – 4,5 kilometer 

Zoek je verkoeling? Dan is deze route door het Spaarbankbos een aanrader. De bomen zijn ruim 100 jaar oud, dus je wandelt grotendeels in de schaduw. Onderweg zie je hoge naaldbossen, natte laagtes en open zandverstuivingen. Een fijne ontsnapping aan de hitte, vlak bij Hoogeveen. 

Groningen | Wandelroute Dollard – 10 kilometer 

Trek je wandelschoenen aan en ontdek de Dollard. Langs de dijk waait bijna altijd een verkoelend briesje. Je geniet van weidse uitzichten, kwelders en broedvogels. Met een beetje geluk zie je zelfs zeehonden op de slikken. 

Utrecht | Klompenpad het Snorrenhoefpad – 7 of 10 kilometer 

Je wandelt grotendeels onder de bomen in de Gelderse Vallei. Onderweg ontdek je het buitengebied van Leusden, met zijn landgoederen, boerenerven en beken. De naam Snorrenhoef verwijst naar het buurtschap dat hier ooit lag. 

Bij boerderij Groot Zandbrink vind je een leuk terras én bijzondere natuur: blauwgraslandjes die uniek zijn in Europa. Deze ontstaan door kwelwater uit diepe bodemlagen. 

Nog meer wandelroutes ontdekken? Ga naar https://www.inhetlandschap.nl/

item.title: Equipping students to be active participants in our democracy
item.description:
When student Landon F. set out to understand why so few of his peers engaged in community activities and other forms of civic life, he found an answer he didn’t expect: His school, Frewsburg Central High School in western New York, offered no civics course. He decided to change that.

Landon organized a student petition committee, cultivated teacher advocates, and eventually presented to his school board. With support from a Carnegie Youth Fellowship through iCivics — a nonprofit that helps schools and students all over America engage in civics education — Landon also interviewed students from across the country about their civics education.

“Hearing how people from all over different parts of the country have different civic experiences is crazy to me,” he said. “You would think there would be a standard to this — civic education requirements, voting, basic engagement, etc. It really makes me think about what we need to do differently.”

Landon’s school isn’t an outlier. In the U.S., civics is often only a single semester in high school, if it’s taught at all, despite research showing that 92% of Americans think civic education is important for our country’s success. Research shows that strong civic learning encourages students to volunteer in their community, advocate for causes they care about, discuss local issues at home, and vote in elections. That’s the foundation that iCivics, a grantee of the Hewlett Foundation’s Education program, is working inside and outside the classroom to give every student in America.

Founded by former Supreme Court Justice Sandra Day O’Connor, iCivics develops free, high-quality educational games, curriculum and classroom tools that help young people understand and participate in democratic life. Every year, its resources reach 9 million students and are used by teachers in 80% of U.S. counties, across school size, in urban and rural districts, and in red, blue, and purple states.

“Civic education is one of the most powerful, underutilized levers we have for protecting human agency and constitutional democracy as the world shifts around us,” said iCivics CEO Louise Dubé. “We must act now to strengthen it on a national scale and reposition it at the center of our education system.”

iCivics designs its curricula to meet students where they are. Its Through Inquiry curriculum has students lead their own learning by asking compelling questions, evaluating primary sources, and completing a capstone project that brings what they’ve learned to life. And because curriculum is only as effective as the teachers who deliver it, iCivics also builds educator capacity through professional development offerings ranging from full courses to immediately actionable workshops.

Beyond curricular and teacher supports, games from iCivics guide students through the democratic process, ensure students understand the history of our nation and the rights they enjoy, demonstrate the consequences of their decisions, and help them develop the civil discourse skills they need to navigate diverse perspectives.

  • In the game Neighborhood Good students step into a fictional neighborhood and pick a local challenge to tackle — such as decreasing food waste or supporting a local animal shelter. They meet with their neighbors, listen to their concerns and ideas, and use what they learn to build a plan to help. Students then see how working together benefits the community’s residents.
  • In Investigation Declaration, students become special agents tasked with redrawing connections between Enlightenment ideas and the Declaration of Independence and identifying how those ideas spread across the Atlantic World over the course of a century.

According to Johns Hopkins research, iCivics resources build students’ critical thinking capacities. They also develop their ability to communicate, collaborate, evaluate information, and be creative — skills that will set them up to succeed in the economy of the future.

After using iCivics resources, students often voice things like: “I didn’t realize I had a role in this.” Teachers share that iCivics games and other tools also encourage students who once hesitated to participate to now raise their hands, engage in class conversations, and dive into their curriculum with excitement.

“No matter what plans students have for life after high school — whatever their career plans, however they may continue their education — all students will be members of communities where they will need agency to raise their voices and make an impact. Civics teaches skills, knowledge, and disposition that will be needed by all,” said Shannon Salter, iCivics Educator Network Teacher.

iCivics is also working outside of classrooms alongside advocates and policymakers to ensure more students are taught these skills. Their CivxNow project, the nation’s largest cross-partisan coalition working to prioritize civic learning in the United States, has encouraged more than 30 states to adopt over 50 civic education policies that teach students interactive and relevant K-12 political participation, civil discourse, and how to engage over disagreements.

At the national level, iCivics and the CivxNow coalition helped triple funding for K–12 civic education programs in the 2023 fiscal year, from $7.75 million to $23 million.

“With civic learning in and out of the classroom and iCivics’ resources and curricula at teachers’ and students’ fingertips, our nation’s young people are better positioned to contribute to the future of their communities, and help build and sustain a durable democracy that works for us all, across our differences,” said Melissa Chabran, Hewlett Foundation Education Program Officer.

The post Equipping students to be active participants in our democracy  appeared first on Hewlett Foundation.
